sections.heading: Flagged items in detail
paragraphs: FCF Generation Consistency: Free cash flow was positive in 1 of the last 5 reported years. Repeated FCF deficits mean growth is being funded by the balance sheet rather than by the business.
Debt-to-Equity Trajectory: Leverage moved from 1.87x to 1.32x equity. Leverage is high enough to transmit an earnings shock directly into equity value.
Current Ratio Liquidity: Current assets cover current liabilities 1.15 times. Liquidity is tight relative to short-term obligations.
Gross Margin Stability: Gross margin varied with a standard deviation of 4.4 percentage points. Margin volatility suggests commodity exposure or weak pricing power.
Operating Margin Stability: Operating margin standard deviation of 4.4 pp indicates cost swings that make forecasting unreliable.
Share Dilution Check: The share count changed +4.1% a year. Dilution transfers value from existing holders to new issuance.
ROE vs. ROCE Quality: Return on capital employed of 6.0% with ROE of 12.3% is close to or below the cost of capital, so growth destroys rather than creates value.
CapEx Intensity Check: Capital expenditure averaged 32.5% of revenue. Capex intensity is unusual for the business model and needs a return check.
Working Capital Cycle (DSO / DIO): The cash conversion cycle absorbs 127 days of working capital. A long cycle ties up cash and makes growth expensive to fund.
Earnings Volatility Check: Earnings per share fell in 0 of the last 4 years with a growth standard deviation of 42 points. Earnings are erratic, which argues for a wider margin of safety.
Interest Coverage Safety: Operating profit covers interest 2.3 times. Coverage is thin enough that a profit dip would pressure debt service.

Auditor & Governance Cleanliness: Aggregating the accounting evidence: 5 hard red flags and 6 watch items, with a LojikX™ Consistency Score of 52/100. The pattern of flags warrants a closer read of the auditor notes and related-party disclosures.
